meta.title: Smart Workout Optimizer (SWO): exercise-level training guidance
meta.description: Wearable-free training guidance. SWO turns sleep quality, fatigue and workout history into exercise-level Green, Amber and Red recommendations.

hero.headline: Know whether to push, hold or ease off, exercise by exercise.
hero.supportingCopy: SWO turns your sleep quality, fatigue and workout history into Green, Amber and Red guidance for each exercise, with the reasoning shown beside every call. No wearable required.

preview.alt: SWO exercise card for a lying leg curl showing an optimal-day message and two suggested next-set targets
preview.caption: Screenshot of the SWO app interface.

problem.heading: Training by feel is guesswork
problem.body: Choosing today's weights from memory and mood is easy. Weighing sleep, soreness and recent sessions against each other, mid-workout, is much harder.
points: Sleep quality shapes how a session feels.
Fatigue and stiffness carry over between workouts.
Last session's numbers are easy to misremember.

howItWorks.heading: From three daily inputs to a call on every exercise
howItWorks.intro: SWO reads what you tell it, compares it with training frameworks, and answers per exercise.

steps.title: Sleep quality
steps.description: Tell SWO how well you slept before you train.

steps.title: Fatigue and stiffness
steps.description: Note how fatigued or stiff you feel, so today's guidance reflects it.

steps.title: Workout performance history
steps.description: Your logged sets and reps give SWO the recent training context.

steps.title: Analysis against frameworks
steps.description: SWO reads your inputs alongside workload, recovery and progression ideas from sports science.

steps.title: Exercise-level guidance
steps.description: Each exercise gets a status, the reason for it and a suggested action.

statuses.label: Optimal zone
statuses.meaning: The exercise sits within SWO's defined training range for today.
statuses.exampleRationale: Example: recovery looks strong and recent sessions on this exercise have been steady, so there is room to progress.
statuses.suggestedAction: Train as planned, or consider a small step up in load or reps.

statuses.label: Caution zone
statuses.meaning: Something in today's inputs suggests adjusting intensity or volume.
statuses.exampleRationale: Example: this muscle is recovered, but overall readiness is moderate, so a lighter session may be wise.
statuses.suggestedAction: Consider reducing the weight or the number of sets.

statuses.label: High-risk flag
statuses.meaning: SWO's rules recommend rest or active recovery for this exercise today.
statuses.exampleRationale: Example: recovery signals and recent training load both point toward holding back on this exercise.
statuses.suggestedAction: Rest, or choose an active-recovery option instead.

features.heading: A call on every exercise, not one score for the day
features.description: A good day for one lift can hide a poor day for another. SWO gives each exercise its own status, so you can adjust where it matters.
bullets: Status shown as text and an icon, never colour alone.
Suggested next-set targets sit beside the reason.

image.alt: SWO exercise card for a lying leg curl with an optimal-day message and suggested weight and rep targets

features.heading: The reason sits beside the status
features.description: When SWO suggests easing off, it says why in plain words and offers a lighter target, so you can judge the call yourself.

image.alt: SWO caution-zone card suggesting a reduced weight, with a short explanation and a lighter suggested set

methodology.heading: The ideas behind the guidance
methodology.intro: SWO draws on established training concepts. Each is described here as a concept first, then as what SWO does with it.

frameworks.name: Acute:chronic workload ratio (ACWR)
frameworks.concept: A published way of comparing recent training load with the load an athlete has been used to over a longer period.
frameworks.swoImplementation: SWO uses this idea as one input when it forms guidance. This page does not claim it predicts injury.

frameworks.name: Fatigue and recovery
frameworks.concept: The idea that training creates fatigue, and that how ready you are reflects the balance between that fatigue and recovery over time.
frameworks.swoImplementation: SWO asks for your sleep quality and fatigue and stiffness so that guidance reflects how recovered you report feeling.

frameworks.name: Progressive overload
frameworks.concept: Gradually raising the demand on the body over time, for example a little more weight or one more rep.
frameworks.swoImplementation: SWO can suggest a next target, such as a slightly heavier load or more reps, when its rules judge a day suitable to progress.

methodology.disclaimer: SWO is a training decision-support tool. It does not diagnose, treat or prevent injury or illness and is not a substitute for professional advice. Its guidance follows the app's own rules and has not been clinically validated.

faq.question: Do I need a wearable to use SWO?
faq.answer: No. SWO is wearable-free. It works from the sleep quality, fatigue and stiffness, and workout history that you provide.

faq.question: What do Green, Amber and Red mean?
faq.answer: Green is the optimal zone, Amber is a caution zone where adjusting intensity or volume may help, and Red is a high-risk flag where SWO recommends rest or active recovery. Every status comes with a label, an icon and a reason.

faq.question: Is SWO medical advice?
faq.answer: No. SWO supports training decisions. It does not diagnose conditions, and it should not replace advice from a qualified professional.

faq.question: Who is SWO for?
faq.answer: SWO is designed for individual gym-goers and serious lifters who want help deciding how hard to train on a given day.

faq.question: Are the screenshots on this page a live product?
faq.answer: The screenshots show the SWO app interface. This page is a marketing preview and is not a live connection to the app.
